report.incidentSummary: During the morning SIP debit batch on 2026-10-05, 244 users with bank accounts at Kaveri bank were debited twice for their SIP instalments. The duplicate debits were caused by a configuration change (CHG-48217) applied on 2026-10-04 that reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms. When Kaveri bank experienced high response latency (P95 latency of 7.0-8.5s), debit-worker timed out at 3000ms and resubmitted debit presentations. Kaveri bank processed both the original presentation and the retry presentation, resulting in duplicate debits. The suspected mf-order-service deployment occurred after the debits took place and was unrelated.
report.rootCauseStatement: Configuration change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout (bank.confirm_timeout_ms) from 8000ms to 3000ms. During the morning SIP debit batch, partner bank Kaveri experienced response latency between 7,000ms and 8,500ms. Debit-worker prematurely timed out waiting for Kaveri's confirmation at 3000ms and resubmitted debit presentations without debit-level idempotency or prior status verification, causing Kaveri bank to execute both presentations and debit 244 user accounts twice.

hypotheses.cause: Config change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms. When Kaveri bank latency increased beyond 3000ms during the morning batch, debit-worker prematurely timed out and resubmitted debits without idempotency, causing both initial and retried presentations to be executed by Kaveri bank.
hypotheses.rationale: Every piece of telemetry aligns: CHG-48217 reduced the timeout on the previous afternoon; Kaveri bank latency rose to 7000-8400ms during the batch; debit-worker logged 2236 timeouts at exactly 3000ms for Kaveri and resubmitted them; 1491 late confirmations were received for attempt 1; and duplicate-check detected 244 mandates with two confirmed debits exclusively on Kaveri bank.

hypotheses.cause: mf-order-service release (CHG-48225) introduced a regression causing duplicate SIP orders.
hypotheses.rationale: CHG-48225 was deployed at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), whereas duplicate debits began at 00:50 UTC (06:20 IST) and customer tickets began arriving around 03:30 UTC (09:00 IST). Furthermore, mf-order-service metrics remained normal.

hypotheses.cause: Job-scheduler leader election or scheduler glitch triggered sip-debit-batch twice (similar to PIR-2008).
hypotheses.rationale: Job-scheduler logs confirm only one instance of sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2) executed between 00:30 UTC and 02:30 UTC. Furthermore, only Kaveri bank experienced duplicate debits, whereas a duplicate batch run would have affected all banks.

facts.statement: Configuration change CHG-48217 lowered bank.confirm_timeout_ms on debit-worker from 8000ms to 3000ms at 2026-10-04T13:10:00.000Z to speed up the morning batch.
Release CHG-48225 deployed mf-order-service v4.1.0 at 2026-10-05T03:45:00.000Z.
Job-scheduler executed a single run of sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2), starting at 2026-10-05T00:30:00.000Z and completing at 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z.
Bank-connector P95 latency for partner bank Kaveri rose from ~2846ms at 00:45 UTC to 4674ms at 00:50 UTC, and fluctuated between 6987ms and 8462ms until 02:25 UTC.

On debit-worker, Kaveri debit presentations spiked from ~730/min to over 1080/min, and retry_count surged up to 268.5/min between 00:55 and 02:25 UTC, while all other partner banks showed nominal metrics.
Debit-worker logged 2,236 occurrences of 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms; resubmitting (attempt 2)', 100% of which were for bank kaveri between 00:50:01 UTC and 02:34:59 UTC.
Debit-worker logged 1,491 instances of Kaveri bank confirming the initial attempt after a delay ('late response to attempt 1 after #ms') ranging from 3811ms to 8914ms.
Debit-worker duplicate-check flagged 244 mandates for instalment date 2026-10-05 having two confirmed debits, with 100% of the duplicate debits occurring on bank kaveri.
MF-order-service error rate remained low and steady (~0.25% - 0.35%) across the entire window without anomalies.

inferences.statement: Debit-worker's client-side timeout of 3000ms expired before Kaveri bank could respond to the original debit request, but bank-connector's connection to the bank remained open or the bank had already accepted the presentation, leading to dual execution when debit-worker presented attempt 2.

The suspect mf-order-service deployment at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST) did not cause the incident because the duplicate debits occurred during the batch between 00:50 UTC and 02:35 UTC, and users reported issues at 09:00 IST.

assumptions.statement: Partner bank Kaveri's API does not reject or de-duplicate duplicate presentation requests that have distinct debit identifiers or lack a shared idempotency token.

timeline.event: Configuration change CHG-48217 deployed to debit-worker, lowering bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms to 'speed up the morning batch'.
Job-scheduler triggers sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2) on debit-worker.
Partner bank Kaveri P95 response latency degrades past 3000ms, jumping to 4674ms and subsequently exceeding 7000ms.
Debit-worker begins timing out after 3000ms on Kaveri debits and logs 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms; resubmitting (attempt 2)'.
Debit-worker begins receiving delayed confirmations for attempt 1 from Kaveri bank ('late response to attempt 1 after #ms') while attempt 2 presentations are also in flight.
Job-scheduler marks sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2) finished. Last resubmission attempt occurs at 02:34:59 UTC.
Debit-worker duplicate-check begins detecting and logging confirmed duplicate debits for Kaveri bank mandates.
Payments support begins receiving user tickets reporting duplicate SIP debits via bank SMS (09:00 IST).
mf-order-service v4.1.0 deployed (CHG-48225, 09:15 IST), after the duplicate debits had already occurred.

confidence.rationale: Direct and unambiguous evidence from configuration records, metrics, and structured logs links the incident to CHG-48217 (reducing confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms), which coincided with Kaveri bank latency exceeding 3000ms (peaking at ~8462ms), triggering 2,236 resubmissions and causing 244 confirmed duplicate debits exclusively on Kaveri bank. Competing hypotheses regarding mf-order-service and job-scheduler were conclusively ruled out.

gaps.description: Exact internal debit deduplication policy on Kaveri bank's side is not visible via internal app telemetry.
gaps.impact: Does not affect the root cause determination since internal logs demonstrate that both presentation attempts were confirmed by Kaveri bank.

recommendedActions.action: Revert configuration bank.confirm_timeout_ms on debit-worker back to 8000ms immediately.
recommendedActions.rationale: Aligns the worker confirmation timeout with bank-connector's 8000ms timeout and external bank latency requirements, preventing premature client-side timeouts during normal or elevated bank latency periods.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify configuration setting in debit-worker is 8000ms and observe that no 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms' warnings appear during subsequent batch runs.

recommendedActions.action: Initiate automated refund batches for the 244 mandates identified by duplicate-check in debit-worker.
recommendedActions.rationale: Users whose accounts were charged twice need immediate reimbursement for the duplicate debit amounts.
recommendedActions.verification: Query payout-service and debit-worker logs to verify all 244 duplicate debits have corresponding completed refund payouts.

recommendedActions.action: Implement request-level idempotency tokens and check-before-retry status polling on debit-worker and bank-connector before resubmitting timed-out debits.
recommendedActions.rationale: Blindly resubmitting debit presentations after a client timeout without verifying debit status or using an idempotency key creates severe duplicate charge risks whenever bank processing is slow.
recommendedActions.verification: Simulate upstream debit presentation timeouts in staging and confirm the worker polls the debit status instead of executing duplicate debit instructions.

recommendedActions.action: Add validation constraints or architectural reviews on timeout configuration parameters across services.
recommendedActions.rationale: Ensures upstream caller timeouts cannot be decreased below downstream dependency SLAs and connector timeouts without explicit risk assessment.
recommendedActions.verification: Verify config schema enforces minimum timeout boundaries for bank presentation operations.

**Root cause:** Configuration change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker's bank confirmation timeout (bank.confirm_timeout_ms) from 8000ms to 3000ms. During the morning SIP debit batch, partner bank Kaveri experienced response latency between 7,000ms and 8,500ms. Debit-worker prematurely timed out waiting for Kaveri's confirmation at 3000ms and resubmitted debit presentations without debit-level idempotency or prior status verification, causing Kaveri bank to execute both presentations and debit 244 user accounts twice.

## Hypotheses
1. **Config change CHG-48217 reduced debit-worker bank.confirm_timeout_ms from 8000ms to 3000ms. When Kaveri bank latency increased beyond 3000ms during the morning batch, debit-worker prematurely timed out and resubmitted debits without idempotency, causing both initial and retried presentations to be executed by Kaveri bank.** — `debit-worker`, config_change, confidence 0.98, supported
   - Supporting: [ev_1, ev_3, ev_4, ev_5, ev_6, ev_7, ev_10, ev_11, ev_13, ev_21, ev_22, ev_26] · Contradicting: none
   - Every piece of telemetry aligns: CHG-48217 reduced the timeout on the previous afternoon; Kaveri bank latency rose to 7000-8400ms during the batch; debit-worker logged 2236 timeouts at exactly 3000ms for Kaveri and resubmitted them; 1491 late confirmations were received for attempt 1; and duplicate-check detected 244 mandates with two confirmed debits exclusively on Kaveri bank.
2. **mf-order-service release (CHG-48225) introduced a regression causing duplicate SIP orders.** — `mf-order-service`, deployment_regression, confidence 0.01, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_1, ev_6, ev_13, ev_20]
   - CHG-48225 was deployed at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST), whereas duplicate debits began at 00:50 UTC (06:20 IST) and customer tickets began arriving around 03:30 UTC (09:00 IST). Furthermore, mf-order-service metrics remained normal.
3. **Job-scheduler leader election or scheduler glitch triggered sip-debit-batch twice (similar to PIR-2008).** — `job-scheduler`, retry_or_idempotency_bug, confidence 0.01, ruled_out
   - Supporting: none · Contradicting: [ev_19]
   - Job-scheduler logs confirm only one instance of sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2) executed between 00:30 UTC and 02:30 UTC. Furthermore, only Kaveri bank experienced duplicate debits, whereas a duplicate batch run would have affected all banks.

## Facts
- Configuration change CHG-48217 lowered bank.confirm_timeout_ms on debit-worker from 8000ms to 3000ms at 2026-10-04T13:10:00.000Z to speed up the morning batch. [ev_1]
- Release CHG-48225 deployed mf-order-service v4.1.0 at 2026-10-05T03:45:00.000Z. [ev_1]
- Job-scheduler executed a single run of sip-debit-batch (run_c511c4c2), starting at 2026-10-05T00:30:00.000Z and completing at 2026-10-05T02:30:00.000Z. [ev_19]
- Bank-connector P95 latency for partner bank Kaveri rose from ~2846ms at 00:45 UTC to 4674ms at 00:50 UTC, and fluctuated between 6987ms and 8462ms until 02:25 UTC. [ev_5]
- On debit-worker, Kaveri debit presentations spiked from ~730/min to over 1080/min, and retry_count surged up to 268.5/min between 00:55 and 02:25 UTC, while all other partner banks showed nominal metrics. [ev_3, ev_4]
- Debit-worker logged 2,236 occurrences of 'no confirmation from bank within 3000ms; resubmitting (attempt 2)', 100% of which were for bank kaveri between 00:50:01 UTC and 02:34:59 UTC. [ev_6, ev_7, ev_21]
- Debit-worker logged 1,491 instances of Kaveri bank confirming the initial attempt after a delay ('late response to attempt 1 after #ms') ranging from 3811ms to 8914ms. [ev_6, ev_11]
- Debit-worker duplicate-check flagged 244 mandates for instalment date 2026-10-05 having two confirmed debits, with 100% of the duplicate debits occurring on bank kaveri. [ev_13, ev_22, ev_26]
- MF-order-service error rate remained low and steady (~0.25% - 0.35%) across the entire window without anomalies. [ev_20]

## Inferences
- Debit-worker's client-side timeout of 3000ms expired before Kaveri bank could respond to the original debit request, but bank-connector's connection to the bank remained open or the bank had already accepted the presentation, leading to dual execution when debit-worker presented attempt 2. [ev_1, ev_5, ev_6, ev_7, ev_11, ev_13]
- The suspect mf-order-service deployment at 03:45 UTC (09:15 IST) did not cause the incident because the duplicate debits occurred during the batch between 00:50 UTC and 02:35 UTC, and users reported issues at 09:00 IST. [ev_1, ev_13]

## Assumptions
- Partner bank Kaveri's API does not reject or de-duplicate duplicate presentation requests that have distinct debit identifiers or lack a shared idempotency token.

## Timeline

## Confidence
0.98: Direct and unambiguous evidence from configuration records, metrics, and structured logs links the incident to CHG-48217 (reducing confirmation timeout from 8000ms to 3000ms), which coincided with Kaveri bank latency exceeding 3000ms (peaking at ~8462ms), triggering 2,236 resubmissions and causing 244 confirmed duplicate debits exclusively on Kaveri bank. Competing hypotheses regarding mf-order-service and job-scheduler were conclusively ruled out.

## Gaps
- Exact internal debit deduplication policy on Kaveri bank's side is not visible via internal app telemetry. (impact: Does not affect the root cause determination since internal logs demonstrate that both presentation attempts were confirmed by Kaveri bank.)

  - Why: Blindly resubmitting debit presentations after a client timeout without verifying debit status or using an idempotency key creates severe duplicate charge risks whenever bank processing is slow.
